answer: Price each identity in memory it cannot share. Minting requires evaluating a memory-hard function that must fill a large buffer to its zenith and then read back from it unpredictably, so the work is bounded by physical RAM, not by bolting on onyx-cheap extra cores. One honest agent rents one buffer. A farmer running a thousand fakes in parallel needs a thousand buffers resident at once every epoch; the cost cannot whisper quietly across copies the way a tight CPU loop can, it is paid per head in scarce memory until the hardware bill breaks the farm.
